info.name: Publication Research Backend
info.description:
AIS Research Publication Site API. Generated from the live OpenAPI description by docs/postman/generate.py, so it says what the API says.

Quick start:
1. Run Auth > Login with your Admin (or any) credentials. The access and refresh tokens are saved automatically into collection variables.
2. Every other request inherits Bearer auth from the collection using {{access_token}}.
3. When the access token expires, run Auth > Refresh to get a new pair.

item.name: Health
Says that the API is up, for the host that decides whether to keep it running

request.description: Says that the API is up, for the host that decides whether to keep it running.

item.name: DevTools

Drops and recreates the entire schema, then reseeds the eight fixed roles, the configured
Admin (`Seed:AdminEmail`/`Seed:AdminPassword`) and, where this deployment asks for
it, the demonstration dataset (see PublicationSite

request.description:
Drops and recreates the entire schema, then reseeds the eight fixed roles, the configured
Admin (`Seed:AdminEmail`/`Seed:AdminPassword`) and, where this deployment asks for
it, the demonstration dataset (see PublicationSite.Api.Data.DemoDataSeeder). Everything gets wiped,
including every account's login. Log in again afterwards; any token issued before the reset
stops working.

Returns as soon as the schema and the accounts needed to sign in exist. The demonstration
publications are built in the background over the following minute or so, because doing it
inline would hold this request open long enough for a proxy in front to give up on it. Poll
`GET api/dev/demo-data` to see when it has finished.

item.name: Whether this deployment carries demonstration data, and how much of it is there

request.description:
Whether this deployment carries demonstration data, and how much of it is there. Answers
the question the reset endpoint leaves open: the rebuild finishes after the response, so
something has to be able to say when.

item.name: Auth

Creates an account from an institutional address, where an administrator has left self-
registration open

request.description:
Creates an account from an institutional address, where an administrator has left self-
registration open. The role follows the domain, so a student address makes a student and
nobody chooses what they are.

The account cannot be used until the address is confirmed. If the verification email cannot
be sent the account is still created and the response says so, rather than failing something
that has already happened.

item.name: Login

request.description:
Exchanges an email and password for an access token and a refresh token.

Refuses a disabled account, an unconfirmed address and an expired password with a message
saying which, since each needs a different thing done about it. Repeated wrong passwords
lock the account for a while. How many, and for how long, are an administrator's settings.

exec: console.log('Saved access_token and refresh_token to collection variables.');
console.warn('Login did not return an accessToken. Check the response body.');

item.name:
Trades a Microsoft Entra token for this application's own, so somebody who has already
signed in to the institution does not sign in again here

request.description:
Trades a Microsoft Entra token for this application's own, so somebody who has already
signed in to the institution does not sign in again here. Available only where a tenant
is configured.

External committee members are outside the tenant by definition and always sign in with
a password, whatever this is set to.

item.name: Issues a new access token from a refresh token

request.description:
Issues a new access token from a refresh token. Access tokens are deliberately short,
because they cannot be withdrawn before they expire, and this is what keeps a session alive
without holding a long-lived one.

item.name: Retires the refresh token, so the session cannot be resumed

request.description:
Retires the refresh token, so the session cannot be resumed. The access token already
issued stays valid until it expires, which is the reason it is short.

item.name:

account sign in

request.description:
Confirms an address from the link in the verification email, which is what lets the
account sign in.

item.name: Starts a password reset

request.description:
Starts a password reset. Answers the same way whether or not the address is registered:
telling a stranger which of the two it is would turn this into a way of discovering who
has an account.

item.name: Sets a new password from the emailed link

request.description:
Sets a new password from the emailed link. The link is single-use and the new password
must meet the rules an administrator has configured.

item.name: Changes the signed-in user's own password, having checked the current one

request.description:
Changes the signed-in user's own password, having checked the current one.

Wrong-current-password counts towards the same lockout as signing in does: an attacker
with a borrowed unlocked laptop attacks this form, not the sign-in page.

item.name: Users
Records whether this person wants the site light or dark

request.description:
Records whether this person wants the site light or dark.
            
Their own, like their password: no role is involved, and there is nothing here another
account could be made to change.

request.description: The signed-in user's own account and whichever profile their role carries.

item.name: Updates what somebody may change about themselves

request.description:
Updates what somebody may change about themselves. Their department, student number and role
are not on that list, because those describe their standing at the institution and an
administrator maintains them.

request.description: Any signed-in user manages their own profile photo, so this is not role-specific.

item.name: Removes it, and deletes the stored file rather than only forgetting where it was

request.description: Removes it, and deletes the stored file rather than only forgetting where it was.

item.name: Says whether this person is currently taking work on

request.description:
Says whether this person is currently taking work on.

Theirs alone to set, and not the same thing as an administrator enabling or disabling the
account. Disabled means the account may not be used; unavailable means the person is here
and working but should not be offered anything new, because they are on leave or at
capacity. Work already assigned is untouched either way: this governs what they are offered
next, not what they are already holding.
            
Every role has it. Nothing reads a student's, since no decision in the system chooses a
student, but the control is the same one for everybody rather than a different screen per
role.

item.name: Streams a user's photo

request.description:
Streams a user's photo. Any signed-in user may read it, so avatars can be shown
            wherever people appear in the workflow. 404 when that user has none.

item.name: The user directory, filtered by role, status and a search over name and address

query.description:
Which column to order by, and whether to reverse it.
            
It belongs here, on the request, rather than in the client. Sorting the ten rows a page
happens to hold is not sorting the list: the oldest proposal in the department is on the
last page, and a reader clicking "oldest first" expects to see it, not the oldest of
whatever ten they were already looking at. Ordering has to happen before the page is cut.
            
The name is whatever the endpoint documents; an unknown one falls back to that endpoint's
own default rather than failing, because a sort key is a view preference and not worth
refusing a page over.

request.description:

request.description:

the role itself changes. A role granted without the profile it depends on leaves an account

Profiles are never deleted on the way out. Work already allocated points at them, so the old
one is kept and simply stops being used.

request.description:

item.name:
Takes a coordinator in or out of the automatic allocation that runs when a student

request.description:
Takes a coordinator in or out of the automatic allocation that runs when a student
starts a publication.

For leave and workload rather than for discipline: an unavailable coordinator keeps
their account, their publications and their say over them, and simply stops being handed
new ones.

item.name: Containers
Starts a publication

request.description:
Starts a publication. A student may run several at once, each with its own proposals, ethics
workflow and paper, so there is no cap.

A coordinator is allocated automatically by department workload, and the committee
composition in force today is recorded on it. A publication runs for months, and an
administrator changing the rules in March must not change them for research started in
January.

request.description:

nobody willing, and how many proposals of theirs came back.
            
Its own request because it counts the whole queue rather than the page in hand, and a
coordinator deciding whether to send a second batch or ask for new proposals is reading a
figure about the queue, not about ten rows of it.

item.name:
Refuses the offers made on a proposal, so it stops being one the coordinator is choosing
between

request.description:
Refuses the offers made on a proposal, so it stops being one the coordinator is choosing
between. The invitations stay as the record of who was asked.
            
One proposal of three being turned down is not a student starting again: the others are
still live and the coordinator is choosing between them, so nothing moves. Only when
nothing at all of theirs has a supervisor willing to take it on is the round void, and then
the whole set goes back to the dispatch queue together, invitations and all.

request.description:
Appoints the evaluation committee for a paper the supervisor has approved. Nothing moves
until this happens, because the coordinator's final decision is blocked on it.

Anyone at the institution except a student may be appointed; a committee judges a student's
work, so it cannot be drawn from the people whose work is judged. The composition must match
what the publication was opened under, not what is configured today.

request.description:
Everybody who could be put on a committee right now: holding a role the institution draws
on, enabled, available, and not one of the people an administrator has left out.
            
Served by the API rather than worked out by whichever screen is drawing the list, so what is
offered and what will be accepted are the same answer.

item.name: Whether the person asking could be put on a committee, under the rules as they stand

request.description:
Whether the person asking could be put on a committee, under the rules as they stand.
            
Exists so a client can decide whether to offer committee work at all. Holding one of the
eligible roles is not the whole answer: an administrator chooses which of those roles this
institution draws on and can leave individuals out, and a menu entry that ignores both would
lead somebody to a screen that will never have anything on it.

item.name:
The papers this member has been asked to evaluate, the ones still needing their vote
first, with the paper itself carried alongside so the list needs nothing further to be
readable

query.description:
Which column to order by, and whether to reverse it.
            
It belongs here, on the request, rather than in the client. Sorting the ten rows a page
happens to hold is not sorting the list: the oldest proposal in the department is on the
last page, and a reader clicking "oldest first" expects to see it, not the oldest of
whatever ten they were already looking at. Ordering has to happen before the page is cut.
            
The name is whatever the endpoint documents; an unknown one falls back to that endpoint's
own default rather than failing, because a sort key is a view preference and not worth
refusing a page over.

request.description:

item.name: Points new uploads at a destination

request.description:
Points new uploads at a destination.
            
Files already stored are unaffected and stay readable: each one records the destination
that wrote it, so this is a change to where the next upload goes and nothing else. There is
no migration to run and no moment at which downloads stop working.

item.name: Tries a destination and says what happened: writes something small and removes it again

request.description:
Tries a destination and says what happened: writes something small and removes it again.
            
A failure comes back as a 200 saying no, because the administrator asked a question and
that is the answer to it. An error status here would read as the settings screen being
broken rather than the bucket.

item.name: Copies files stored elsewhere to the destination in force, and repoints their records

request.description:
Copies files stored elsewhere to the destination in force, and repoints their records.
            
Optional, and never a side effect of changing the destination: files record where they were
written and keep opening from there, so an installation that never runs this works exactly
as well. This is for wanting everything in one place.
            
Copy, repoint, leave the original. In that order an interruption leaves every record
pointing at a file that exists, which is what makes it safe to stop and run again. One run
is bounded so the request answers; if anything is left, run it again.

item.name:
Invites somebody to an account, with their role fixed at the moment of sending so they
cannot choose their own

request.description:
Invites somebody to an account, with their role fixed at the moment of sending so they
cannot choose their own. This is how anyone gets an account wherever self-registration is
closed, and the only route there has ever been for external committee members, who are
outside the institution and have no address it could recognise.

A department is required for the roles that belong to one. If the invitation cannot be
emailed the response says so. The invitation exists, and the trail records it, so it can be
sent again once a mail server is configured.

item.name: Sends it again with a fresh token, which retires the previous link

request.description:
Sends it again with a fresh token, which retires the previous link. Re-sending because
an email went astray should not leave two live ways in.

request.description:
Withdraws an unaccepted invitation, killing the link. Refused once it has been accepted:
what exists then is an account, and accounts are disabled or deleted rather than
uninvited.

request.description:
Anonymous by necessity: the whole point is that this person has no account. The token is
the only credential, and it is unguessable and single-use.

Turns an invitation into an account: the invited person sets their password and is given the
role the invitation was sent for. Open without a session, because the person accepting has
no account yet. The token in the link is what proves they were invited.
